verdict_reasoning: The goal is sound: the planner should use expression statistics that match a COLLATE expression. The design is not settled. standards-compat-2 shows the v6 retry may match statistics built under a different collation, and maintenance-fit-3 shows the thread states no single matching rule. Planning cost is unmeasured for v6 after the cost objection in message #3 (maintenance-fit-1), and the stable target is not argued (standards-compat-1).

brief.title: Planner ignores collation when matching expression statistics in examine_variable
brief.problem: examine_variable strips every top-level RelabelType from the expression, including the one a COLLATE clause becomes. So a query that groups by `a COLLATE case_insensitive` uses the plain column statistics and not the extended statistics on that expression. In the author's demo the estimate is 52 rows and the actual count is 32. This affects users of nondeterministic collations and of expression statistics.
brief.proposed_design: v1 changes the RelabelType handling in examine_variable in selfuncs.c. From v2 on, the reviewer Zizhuan Liu rewrote the patch. v6 first looks for an exact equal() match against index and statistics expressions, and only then retries with the top RelabelType stripped. It also merges adjacent RelabelTypes when strip_all_phvs_mutator removes PlaceHolderVars.
user_visible_surface: Changed row estimates for queries with COLLATE on columns or expressions that have extended statistics or expression indexes.
author_claims: With v1, the demo estimate changes from 52 rows to 32 rows, which matches the actual count.
v3 replaces a second eval_const_expressions call with an in-place walker that should cost much less.
v5 keeps the pre-7e9f852a lookup behaviour as a fallback, for compatibility.
A reviewer measured no change in planning time for varchar columns with v5.
brief.thread_state: Tom Lane called the v2 approach of a second eval_const_expressions call too expensive. Shihao Zhong found two estimate regressions, and v6 claims to fix both and restore the tests, but nobody has reviewed v6 yet.
unclear: The material does not say whether v6 still fixes the original 52 versus 32 demo from message 1.
Nobody shows planning-time numbers for v6 or for the new walker.
The entry targets stable branches, but the thread does not say which branches have the bug or whether a back-patch is safe.
No reply comes from the original author, Jian He, or from Richard Guo, the author of strip_all_phvs_deep.
Message 1 suggests moving check_estimated_rows to test_setup.sql, and the thread does not say whether v6 does this.

objections.title: Fallback match may reuse statistics built under another collation
objections.failure_scenario: A user creates statistics on (a COLLATE case_insensitive) and runs GROUP BY a COLLATE "C". The exact match fails, and the retry strips the top RelabelType on both sides, so the two expressions match. The planner then uses the case-insensitive ndistinct of 32 for a grouping that returns 52 groups, which is the bug from message #1 in reverse.
objections.argument: Message #1 argues that ndistinct under one collation does not hold under another. Messages #7 and #9 keep the old strip-and-compare as a fallback for compatibility, and from v6 it also runs when only the statistics expression has a COLLATE. Nothing in the thread says whether the retry checks that the stripped collations agree, or limits itself to deterministic collations, where the statistics would be the same.
objections.author_must_show: When the retry strips a COLLATE from either side, does it check that the collations used by the query and the statistics agree, or are both deterministic?

critic.reasoning: Message #7 says the retry strips the top RelabelType from both sides, and no message mentions a collation check. The stripping for non-Var expressions predates this patch, but whether v6 extends it to plain columns cannot be checked without the code.

objections.title: Planning cost of v6 two-pass lookup is not measured
objections.failure_scenario: A user plans many queries on varchar columns, whose Vars carry an implicit top-level RelabelType, against tables with several expression indexes and statistics objects. v6 compares every index and statistics expression twice when no exact match exists, and also runs a new walker inside strip_all_phvs_mutator. Planning time rises for users who never wrote COLLATE.
objections.argument: examine_variable runs for nearly every clause and grouping expression the planner estimates. In message #3, Tom Lane objected to the cost of v2. The only measurement, in message #8, covers v5 on varchar columns with no index or statistics expressions present. v6 changed the retry conditions and was not measured.
objections.author_must_show: What does planning time look like with v6 for varchar and text columns on tables with many expression indexes and statistics objects, with and without PlaceHolderVars?

critic.reasoning: The only measurement is Shihao Zhong's in message #8, for v5 on varchar columns. v6 changed the retry conditions, and nobody measured it or the new walker after Tom Lane's cost objection in message #3.

objections.title: Back-patching a planner estimate change to stable branches
objections.failure_scenario: A site with expression statistics or expression indexes on COLLATE expressions installs a minor release. Row estimates for those queries change, for example 52 to 32 or 100 to 26, and some plans flip. The site finds out from slower queries after the update, with no setting to turn the change off.
objections.argument: The CommitFest entry targets stable, but every version since message #6 changes which statistics a COLLATE query matches. Messages #6 and #8 show that each version so far moved estimates for tables the patch did not aim at. Minor releases normally avoid changes to plans unless a wrong result or a crash forces one. The thread does not say which branches have the bug or why a back-patch is worth the plan churn.
objections.author_must_show: Which stable branches give the wrong estimate, and why should a plan-changing estimate fix go there instead of master only?

critic.reasoning: The CommitFest entry targets stable, and the thread does not name the affected branches or argue for a back-patch. Messages #6 and #8 show estimates moving for cases the patch did not aim at, so the plan-change risk is concrete.

objections.title: Ad hoc matching rules in examine_variable without an engaged owner
objections.failure_scenario: A later patch changes how expressions in index or statistics definitions are normalized, for example how CollateExpr is stripped. That patch has to keep the exact pass, the retry pass and the per-side RelabelType flags consistent. If it misses one, estimates change without any test failing, and users report it releases later.
objections.argument: v6 adds three flags that decide which comparisons the retry runs. The retry keeps the old behaviour from before 7e9f852a as a compatibility fallback, and the thread does not state the rule it implements. Each of v4, v5 and v6 fixed a case the previous version broke, which shows the rules are easy to get wrong. The original author has been silent since message #1, Richard Guo was CC'd in message #4 and did not reply, and no committer has reviewed the rewrite.
objections.author_must_show: Can the rule for when an expression matches statistics be stated once, so that index and statistics normalization and examine_variable share one helper and do not diverge?

critic.reasoning: Message #9 describes three per-side flags, and the thread states no single matching rule. The silence of the original author and Richard Guo is a committability point and should not add weight to the design objection.

refuted.title: Back-patching estimate changes risks plan flips in minor releases
refuted.failure_scenario: A user on a stable branch upgrades to a minor release. Queries that use COLLATE on columns with expression statistics or indexes get new row estimates, and a join or aggregate plan changes. The user finds out from a slower query in production, with no setting to get the old behaviour back.
refuted.argument: The CommitFest entry targets stable branches. The thread does not say which branches have the problem, and the problem looks like an estimate quality issue rather than a wrong result. Shihao Zhong found two estimate regressions in versions that already looked correct (messages #6 and #8). That shows how easily this code moves plans that users depend on.
refuted.author_must_show: Which branches have the problem, and why should a change that only alters row estimates go into minor releases instead of master only?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-1, which states the same back-patch concern with more specific evidence.

refuted.title: Back-patching estimate changes needs field demand the thread does not show
refuted.failure_scenario: A site on a stable minor release runs queries with `a COLLATE "C" = 'A'` or a similar plain-column COLLATE and has no extended statistics. After a minor upgrade, a change in the lookup order alters its row estimates and some plans flip. The site finds out from slower queries, with no release-note entry it would have linked to its workload.
refuted.argument: The CommitFest entry targets stable branches. The only evidence of the bug is the constructed demo in message #1; no user report appears. The lookup path is shared by every COLLATE query, and v1 and v4 already changed estimates for tables without statistics objects (messages #6 and #8). The benefit goes to the few users with expression statistics on COLLATE expressions, while the risk of an estimate change in a minor release falls on everyone who writes COLLATE.
refuted.author_must_show: Which users hit this misestimate in production, and why must the fix go to stable branches and not only to master?

critic.reasoning: Message #8 confirms that v5 restores rows=100 for the plain-column COLLATE case without statistics, so the stated scenario no longer occurs. The remaining back-patch concern duplicates standards-compat-1, and a reproducible misestimate that ignores user-created statistics needs no field report.

touch_points.reason: The patch changes which statistics examine_variable matches for COLLATE expressions, so row estimates and plans change.

touch_points.reason: The CommitFest entry targets stable, and the change alters row estimates in minor releases.

touch_points.reason: v6 adds an exact pass, a retry pass and per-side RelabelType flags that later normalization changes must keep consistent.

questions: When the v6 retry strips a top RelabelType from either side, does it check that the query collation and the statistics collation agree, or that both are deterministic?
Does v6 still change the message #1 demo estimate from 52 to 32 rows?
What is the planning time with v6 for varchar and text columns on tables with many expression indexes and statistics objects, with and without PlaceHolderVars?
Which stable branches give the wrong estimate, and why should a plan-changing estimate fix go there instead of master only?

committability.owner_note: It needs a committer who knows selfuncs.c and extended statistics matching. Tom Lane objected once to the cost of v2 in message #3, and no committer has commented on v3 to v6.
committability.liability: The committer signs for every estimate change on COLLATE queries, in back branches too if the stable target stays, and for keeping the two-pass matching rules consistent with index and statistics normalization.
committability.author_follow_up: The original author has not replied since message #1. The reviewer Zizhuan Liu wrote v2 to v6 and answered each reported regression, which suggests he stays for fixes.

priority.reason: The fix helps users who combine COLLATE expressions with expression statistics or indexes, and it changes a planner path that every query uses. The patch is small, but v4, v5 and v6 each fixed a regression from the previous version, and no code was read for this review.

provisional_note: Without the code, this review cannot confirm whether the v6 retry compares collations, how much the second pass and the walker cost, or whether new helper signatures affect a back-patch.

precedents_retrieved.title: Extended statistics / estimate Var op Var clauses
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch series lets the planner use extended statistics (MCV lists) to estimate (Var op Var) clauses such as a < b, which before were estimated only for (Var op Const). It also improves selfuncs estimates for clauses with the same expression on both sides, such as a = a, and changes which clauses count as "simple" in the MCV OR handling.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Dean Rasheed's July 2022 review found that the change to "issimple" handling makes some estimates worse, for example WHERE a = 1 OR (b > 0 AND b < 10), and no existing regression test caught this. He asked whether that part was still needed after the selfuncs fixes. The author did not answer for two months, so Michael Paquier marked the entry Returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: The patch changes that, which ends up making things worse in some cases.

precedents_retrieved.title: Support regular expressions with nondeterministic collations
precedents_retrieved.summary: Allow regular expression functions and operators with nondeterministic collations by ignoring the collate part of the collation and keeping only its ctype behaviour. SIMILAR TO patterns, which the SQL standard defines in terms of the collation, get an internal "***S" prefix so they still raise an error under a nondeterministic collation.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected that the patch adds no functionality and forecloses a later, collation-aware definition, and he asked to first check whether the SQL committee knew how to implement its SIMILAR TO definition. The committee had no consensus on the right semantics. Discussion then turned to case-folding approaches for case-insensitive collations, and Peter Eisentraut withdrew the patch in favour of special-purpose collations such as "normal but case insensitive".
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
It adds no
functionality, and it forecloses the possibility of changing
the definition later.

precedents_retrieved.title: Permute underscore separated components of columns before fuzzy matching
precedents_retrieved.summary: Extend the fuzzy column-name matching behind the "Perhaps you meant" hint so that it also checks permutations of up to three underscore-separated words. A swap of two words costs the same as one mistyped character, and the permutation is skipped when the typed name has more than six underscores.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected that the patch adds opaque, almost undocumented code to the matching function, and he doubted that many users want this behavior. He also noted that adjacent underscores and leading or trailing underscores are not handled well. The visible messages show no reply from the author after this review, and the entry was returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
However, we *do*
need to be concerned about its maintainability, and I think the patch
falls down badly there: it adds a chunk of very opaque and essentially
undocumented code, that people will need to reverse-engineer anytime
they are studying this function.

precedents_retrieved.title: Self contradictory examining on rel's baserestrictinfo
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a separate planner pass that examines a relation's baserestrictinfo for self-contradictory quals (btree strategy operators, <>, NULL tests, boolean tests, ScalarArrayOp and row comparisons) and marks the relation dummy. The pass also simplifies redundant quals, such as reducing a <= 10 and a = 10 to a = 10.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Much of the contradiction detection already exists through constraint_exclusion = on and predtest.c, and Tom Lane questioned whether the remaining cases are common enough to justify the added planner cycles. He asked the author to integrate the work with predtest.c and indxpath.c, and not to add a separate analysis pass of a few thousand lines. The patch also lacked comments and changed existing regression tests in ways that would need analysis. Tom Lane returned it because he did not expect anything close to it to be committed.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
So in short, my main review comment is that you should be looking
to integrate with existing planner functionality such as predtest.c
and indxpath.c, rather than writing a few thousand lines of
not-connected-to-anything-else code.  It's too hard to make the
case that these optimizations are worth the cost if they require
an entire separate analysis pass.

precedents_retrieved.title: Make selectivity example match wording
precedents_retrieved.summary: The doc patch changes the unique, non-null join selectivity example so that it divides by the maximum of the two row counts, as the prose describes, and uses num_rows in place of num_distinct. A v2 patch also rewrote the explanation of the formula in the docs and in the code comments, including the proof in the comments.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. The reviewer called the smaller change valuable and was "good" apart from one wording suggestion. The thread then has no further messages before the entry was returned with feedback in November.

precedents_retrieved.title: estimating joins using extended statistics
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch uses multi-column MCV lists from extended statistics to estimate equijoin selectivity, matching the MCV lists of the two joined relations the way eqjoinsel_inner does. It can also use base restrictions as conditions on the MCV lists, and estimates joins of more than two relations one relation pair at a time.
precedents_retrieved.objection: No reviewer objected to the design in the visible messages. The last messages report that the 2022-01-01 version fails cfbot with uninitialized-variable warnings in mcv_combine_simple() and no longer applies to master, and no new version appears before the entry was returned. The author still listed open items, such as no support for outer or inequality joins and possibly wrong ndistinct and nullfract assumptions for column subsets.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Also the patch doesn't apply anymore:

precedents_retrieved.title: Improve planner cost estimations for alternative subplans
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Melanie Plageman, Tomas Vondra, Tom Lane
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changes how the planner costs an AlternativeSubPlan (hashed or per-row lookup) for the rest of the query. It replaces the use of the per-row estimate with a heuristic blend of the two alternatives' costs.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers said that averaging the costs of two alternatives is wrong in principle, because at run time the executor uses one of them. Tomas Vondra expected regressions where the first plan is used, and the author then found queries that ran slower with the patch. The author suggested moving to Tom Lane's approach of passing a number-of-evaluations estimate to cost_qual_eval, or to Andy Fan's proof of concept that picks the SubPlan during planning, and the entry was withdrawn.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I agree that averaging together the costs of the alternatives seems
wrong in principle.  It's going to be one or the other, not some
quantum-mechanical superposition.

precedents_retrieved.summary:

Reverted commit(s): Read extension script files in text not binary mode.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Revert commit 924e03917 in favor of adding code to convert \r\n to \n
explicitly, on Windows only.  The idea of letting text mode do the
work fails for a couple of reasons:

* Per Microsoft documentation, text mode also causes control-Z to be
interpreted as end-of-file.  While it may be unlikely that extension
scripts contain control-Z, we've historically allowed it, and breaking
the case doesn't seem wise.

* Apparently, on some Windows configurations, "r" mode is interpreted
as binary not text mode.  We could force it with "rt" but that would
be inconsistent with our code elsewhere, and it would still require
Windows-specific coding.

Thanks to Alexander Lakhin for investigation.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found: the precedent search returned no earlier rejected, returned, withdrawn or reverted attempt at this idea. Message #7 cites commit 7e9f852a as the change that added the stripping v6 revisits, but the thread does not report it as rejected or reverted.
Both objections are fixable. The proposal adds no syntax, GUC, catalog object or dump format, so pg_dump round-trip, psql conventions and the SQL standard are not affected.

The patch changes only planner estimation logic in selfuncs.c and regression tests. It adds no on-disk format, WAL record, catalog column, wire protocol message or persistent state, so this angle has nothing to object to. Back-patch ABI risk depends on whether new helper signatures are exported, which cannot be checked without code.

This proposal only changes how examine_variable in selfuncs.c matches a query expression against index and extended statistics expressions. It does not change who can create statistics, read them, or run anything, so it adds no privilege model, no new object and no new code path that runs user-controlled code as another role. The existing checks on whether a user may use statistics through operators that are not leakproof sit outside the matching step, and the proposal does not say the patch touches them. Without the code I could not check that the new retry path still goes through those checks.
The goal of using matching expression statistics is reasonable. The objections are about cost, back-patching and how hard the matching rules are to maintain.

This is a bug fix to how examine_variable matches expression statistics. No existing feature, setting or extension lets the planner use expression statistics defined with a COLLATE clause. Users can only avoid writing COLLATE, which changes query semantics, so this angle has nothing to raise.
The fix repairs a lookup that misses existing expression statistics, so it is desirable for master. The objection is limited to the stable-branch target, where no field demand is shown.
